title: The sun is a morning star
word: The sun is a morning star
hookLine: the sun is but a morning star; there is more day to dawn (Walden 18)
last: TRUTH BEFORE LOVE, MONEY AND FAME.

cards: An old kitchen table made of apple-tree wood. Years of meals, elbows, spilled milk. Then one day the family hears a gnawing inside it, and a bug chews its way out of the dry wood, alive and beautiful.
The egg, the story goes, had been laid in the living tree long before it became a table, and it waited all that time. Thoreau tells this on the last pages of Walden as a little resurrection.
Then he ends the book with a few short sentences about the dawn.

teach.h: LIGHT THAT PUTS OUT OUR EYES.
teach.b: Walden's last lines: "The light which puts out our eyes is darkness to us. Only that day dawns to which we are awake. There is more day to dawn. The sun is but a morning star." First, too much light.
A light bright enough to blind you is, to you, the same as dark. Some truths arrive too big to see all at once. Second, the day you're awake for.

teach.h: ONLY THE DAY WE'RE AWAKE TO.
teach.b: A sunrise happens whether you notice or not, but only that day dawns to which we are awake. The calendar can say morning while a person is still asleep inside.
Third, more day to dawn. After a whole book of mornings at the pond, he says the day isn't finished arriving.

teach.h: THE SUN IS BUT A MORNING STAR.
teach.b: Fourth, the sun is but a morning star. A morning star is the bright point you see before sunrise, a sign the day is near.
Thoreau takes the biggest light there is and calls it only a sign of a brighter day still on its way.
It's a strange, hopeful ending: no summary, no moral, a sunrise demoted to a herald, and the bug in the table still fresh in mind, life that waited in dry wood and came out when it was ready.

how: Readers often return to the last lines of Walden as a morning reading: a reminder to be awake for the day that is actually arriving, and that more of it is still to come.

practice: Turn toward the brightest light in reach: an east window if it's morning, a lamp or the sky at any other hour, or the memory of one dawn you were actually awake for.
Don't look straight at the sun; just watch the light change, or hold still. Let the line sit under your breath: there is more day to dawn.

wordCard.voice: The sun is a morning star. Thoreau's last image in Walden: even the sun is only a sign of a bigger day still coming. Today's word.
